name: AutoVerus
org: Microsoft Research, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Columbia University and UC Irvine
one_liner: LLM agents write the proof annotations Verus needs to prove Rust code correct, and Verus's error messages drive the repair rounds.

loop.proposes: Proof annotations (loop invariants, assertions) for Rust code with Verus specifications, from GPT-4o agents
loop.judged_by: The Verus verifier, which either proves the specification or returns errors
loop.steers: Three phases: initial proof, refinement with generic tips, then agents that fix the specific errors Verus reports

headline_result: Proves 137 of 150 tasks (91.3%) on Verus-Bench, with at most 3 tries per task and GPT-4o; 122 were proved on the first attempt. A baseline that repeatedly calls GPT-4o for up to 10 minutes proved 67 of 150. More than half were done in under 30 seconds or 3 LLM calls.
caveat: Verus-Bench is a 150-task suite the authors built from existing code and verification benchmarks, and the task gives the code and the specification. The tool proves what the spec says; a wrong spec would still pass.
beyond_harness_note: Verus decides validity, not an LLM or a test, and the verified annotations stay in the code with no model needed to re-check them.
generative_model: GPT-4o (frozen), orchestrated as a network of specialized agents

sources.title: AutoVerus: Automated Proof Generation for Rust Code
